params.body:
## What

`stocklist:hexon_import` imported every make of a file someone had to place on the public disk first, and wrote at once. It now fetches Hexon's reference list itself, reports before it writes, and writes only what it is told to.

- **Source.** Without a path the list comes from `https://www.doorlinkenvoorraad.nl/ref/makemodels.json?category=AUTO` through the HTTP client (timeout 20 s). Outside production that read is sealed unless `hexonref` is in `OUTBOUND_ALLOW` (new entry in `Outbound::services()`, read half only); the command then says so and stops. A list that is unreachable, answers an error status, is not JSON or is not `[{make, models: [{model}]}]` is an error and nothing is written. The `path` argument still works and needs no open seal.
- **Dry run by default.** `--apply` writes, and wants `--make=<make>` (repeatable) or `--all`; without either it refuses before fetching anything.
- **Matching the way people read it.** Hexon writes `Citroën`, `Škoda`, `Mégane`, `Doblò`; our rows say `Citroen`, `Skoda`, `Megane`, `Doblo`. Compared on the letters, a run over the whole list would have created a second Citroën with 53 models, a second Škoda, and a Mégane beside Megane. Makes are now matched without case, spacing, hyphens or accents, plus the `Volkswagen` to `VW` alias; models without case, spacing or accents. The alias list lives in one place, `App\Support\MakeNames`.
- **Decisions are not guessed.** A make we do not have that resembles one we do (same first word, or one letter apart), or that is a known sub-brand (`Mercedes-AMG`, `DS`), is listed under "Needs a decision" and written only when named with `--make`.
- **Output.** Only what is new is listed, in groups: new makes, new models under makes we have, needs a decision. What matched under another spelling and what already existed is counted. After that, what the import leaves empty for a person: the RealGarant code on make and model, the model type (every model is created as a car), the Modix id, the system code.

## What stays as it was

The accent folding is the import's own key (`ModelNames::unaccented`, used by the command and by `MakeNames`). `ModelNames::normalize`, the comparison behind R S1-3.22, is untouched: `stocklist:merge-duplicate-models` and the chassis lookup (`OwnStockService::mapModel`) compare as before. Whether two existing rows that differ only by an accent should be merged is a separate question, to be answered after counting such rows on production; it is not part of this pull request.

The partner API does not map names: a partner sends the identifiers it read from our lists. So whatever row the import matches or creates is the row the API recognises, and there was no second alias table to keep in step.

## Rules

- R S1-3.24 (new): the import, its source, the dry run, `--make` and `--all`, the matching, the decisions, what stays to fill in.
- R S1-3.22 is unchanged; the import's accent folding is described in R S1-3.24.

## Tests

`HexonReferenceImportTest` (Http::fake, a fixture cut from the list of 1 October 2026): the dry run writes nothing and lists Geely with three models; `--apply --make=Geely` creates one make and three models; a second run creates nothing; `--apply` without `--make` or `--all` refuses; the whole list over our spelling creates no second Citroën, Škoda or VW and no second Mégane, Scénic, Doblò, ë-C3 or Méhari; DS and Mercedes-AMG wait for a decision and are created when named; an unknown make is an error with near matches; a sealed environment refuses; six kinds of bad answer are errors; the path argument still works. `ModelNamesTest` pins the import key (accents fold), the make key, and that the general key still tells accents apart.


Run locally: the import tests, `ModelNamesTest`, `MergeDuplicateModelsTest`, `OutboundTest`, the `Rules*` tests, `QualityRatchetTest`, `LanguageParityTest` and the other tests that touch the outbound catalogue or the model lookup, all green; PHPStan without errors; pint on the new files. The full suite: 2,679 tests, no failures (1 skipped, 1 incomplete), run before the last rebase onto main; the listed classes and PHPStan again after it.
params.title: The Hexon import fetches its list, reports first and matches names as people read them
